outlook: Prices shown are Friday's settlements; no reliable overnight quotes were available this morning. Early commentary said corn and soybeans were higher and wheat was under pressure in Sunday night trade, with positioning ahead of Tuesday's USDA WASDE report and fund money flow the main drivers. Last week was rough: January soybeans fell 40½ cents to $11.93¾ after a nine-day losing streak, December corn lost 6¼ cents to $4.41½ after touching a four-month low, and December Chicago wheat dropped 12¼ cents to $5.91¼, its lowest since late June, as Russia–Ukraine talks weighed on wheat. China kept buying U.S. soybeans (136,000 tonnes announced Friday), and the Canadian dollar weakened to about C$1.41 per US$.
